title: Is this alloc shared memory?
prompt: Your compiler has to decide which allocs are shared memory. uses has one entry for each load or store of one alloc: the number of the global loop that load or store is inside, or None when it is outside every global loop. The list is never empty. Write shared(uses): true when every use is inside the same global loop. The starter says yes to everything.
starter:
def shared(uses: list[int | None]) -> bool:
    return True
hints: Look at the first use. If it is None, the answer is already no.
Every other use must equal the first one. Loop over the list and return False at the first one that differs.
return uses[0] is not None and all(u == uses[0] for u in uses)
explain: An alloc is a block's shared memory when every load and store of it sits inside one and the same global loop. So the first use must be inside a global loop, and every other use must name that same loop. A use outside every global loop, or uses in two different global loops, make it ordinary memory that is not re-zeroed for each block.
